summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory with the sticky bit (mode 1777, owned root:root), verified users can create files but cannot delete or overwrite files owned by other users. Completed mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, restarted node1, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified /srv/drop's permissions and sticky-bit behavior after reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (Ubuntu 16.04) and confirmed /srv/drop did not exist
Created /srv/drop with sudo mkdir, chown root:root, chmod 1777
Created two test users (dropuser1, dropuser2) and verified both could write new files into /srv/drop
Verified dropuser2 could not rm or overwrite dropuser1's file (Operation not permitted / Permission denied) due to sticky bit
Cleaned up test files and removed test users
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and /srv/drop permissions/ownership
Issued sudo shutdown -r now on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified /srv/drop persisted with correct 1777 root:root permissions after reboot
Re-ran the sticky-bit cross-user delete test post-reboot to confirm behavior persisted, then cleaned up test users/files

evidence.requirement: Baseline: /srv/drop created with sticky bit, world-writable, root-owned
evidence.summary: Confirmed /srv/drop did not exist beforehand, then created it and verified mode 1777 (drwxrwxrwt) owned by root:root

evidence.requirement: Functional proof: users can write shared files but cannot remove/overwrite others' files
evidence.summary: Created two test users; both wrote files into /srv/drop successfully; dropuser2's attempt to rm or truncate dropuser1's file failed with Operation not permitted / Permission denied, proving sticky-bit restricted deletion

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of test artifacts before restart
evidence.summary: Removed test files and test users, confirmed /srv/drop remained at 1777 root:root

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fa1e87e6-00f3-42d2-acc5-ad1df6c3d16a and confirmed /srv/drop healthy (1777 root:root, empty)
Issued shutdown -r now (ack returned before disconnect), observed connection refused while rebooting, then successful reconnect

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (actual restart, not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id a9cc3bf2-fcae-4d62-9d85-8b177b8048ce differs from pre-restart fa1e87e6-00f3-42d2-acc5-ad1df6c3d16a, and uptime shows a fresh boot time

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and sticky-bit behavior
evidence.summary: Confirmed /srv/drop still 1777 root:root after reboot; re-ran cross-user delete test showing Operation not permitted, proving sticky-bit behavior persisted across restart; test artifacts cleaned up
